Q: Can the OoO scheduler squash pending instructions (issued by earlier validations) based on predictable behavior? A:

I found the answer:
https://llvm.org/docs/Atomics.html#monotonic
monotonic is the basic reordering constrain in all CPUs.
Monotonicism is how that compiler manual calls it... but during D&R (decode and rename) ... you will see it in action occurring in all hardwares.
The literature is not explicit about the name given to this reordering constrain.... but once you understand the behavior you'll see "monotonicism" materialize.

Basically, I was correct:
There IS a per-address sequential consistency.
Where no RAW and WAR issues will ever happen inside the D&R engine... its own behavior prevents just that.

This means that opaque/relaxed loads WILL NEVER be pre-issued BEFORE the first RMW occurring TO THE SAME ADDRESS:

someOps();
while (exp == V.loadRelaxed()) { 
   if (V.weakRMWRelease(exp, set)) return true; // ^^ (upward barrier)
}

What OoO may do in that scenario is:

  1. V.loadRelaxed();
  2. someOps();
  3. V.RMW
  4. V.loadRelaxed();
  5. V.RMW
    ... etc... etc.

So... Only the VERY FISRT loadRelaxed() is the one that will be allowed to move freely between the first RMW and everything ABOVE/before it.

Q: How to get an older project to Create universal binary and target Apple Silicon A:

Ok, I figured this out finally. The key was in this article from Apple:

https://developer.apple.com/documentation/technotes/tn3117-resolving-build-errors-for-apple-silicon#Unset-Valid-Architectures

It seems that Xcode deprecated the setting VALID_ARCHS, but when opening older projects, it unhelpfully copies that setting into user-defined settings. You have to find that entry under targets>build settings>your target>User-Defined, and kill it with fire (a.k.a. delete it.)

Q: Compiling RPGLE program from IFS path using VScode , for a custom library list A:

You're trying to compile from the IFS, so you don't use actions.json for IFS compiles. You use the typical Actions editor that is part of the UI.

https://codefori.github.io/docs/developing/actions/#_top

You only use actions.json when you are compiling code from your local workspace.
